chunk_findings.detail: `lost` is computed as `len(SS.orphans(events)) - len({e.data["adopted_from"] for e in events if e.data.get("adopted_from")})`. The subtrahend is the number of *distinct `adopted_from` values across all events*, not the number of orphan events that have actually been adopted. Adoption attaches orphans to "the nearest session by time", so several orphans commonly get adopted into the *same* session and therefore carry the same `adopted_from` value; distinct-count then under-counts the adopted set. Concretely, with 3 prompt/note events that `SS.orphans()` still reports (no session id) and all three adopted from/into session S, the set is `{"S"}` (size 1) and `lost = 3 - 1 = 2`, so doctor emits a stale "2 prompt/note event(s) have no session id" warning even though the orphans were already adopted. The dual case (adoption markers on events that are *not* prompt/note orphans, e.g. the adopting session's own events) inflates the subtrahend and can drive `lost <= 0`, silently suppressing the warning for genuinely lost events. Either way the count must be taken over the adopted *event* set, not `set`-deduplicated `adopted_from` values (and restricted to the relevant event types).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting.py:_orphan_notes

chunk_findings.detail: `prompt` still short-circuits on `harness_session_id(harness_id)` *before* consulting `resolve`, so whatever id arrives in `harness_id` is used verbatim and the rules implemented in `resolve` — in particular "the harness id is only accepted when it is still an **open** session (`if hid and hid in live`)" — are bypassed for that id. Concrete case: the autocapture hook / environment supplies the harness session id (`DDFLOW_SESSION_ID` / `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID`, the id B-prompt-autocapture keys on) for a session that already has a `session.ended` event (e.g. `ddflow session end` was run and the shell keeps emitting prompts). `harness_session_id(harness_id)` is truthy, so `resolve` is never called; the prompt is written with that ended session's subject, violating the stated acceptance rule "an ended session is never reused" and the guarantee that the id used is an open/latest/implicit session. Had the call been `resolve(log, harness_id)[0]` (or `resolve(log)[0]` with the explicit id passed through), `resolve` would have rejected the ended id and fallen back to the latest open session or opened an implicit one; the two code paths now disagree about the same input.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `adopt-orphans` branch dereferences the backend result without checking `out.exit`, unlike every other session subcommand in the same function (`start`, `prompt`/`note`) which do `if out.exit != OK: print(out.reason ...); return out.exit`. The method is called as `out = A.session_adopt_orphans(...)`, then the very next line forces `out.data['adopted']` into an f-string and unconditionally `return OK`. If `session_adopt_orphans` returns a non-OK result (e.g., the store/repo cannot be opened or an event is malformed, which is exactly the failure mode the sibling calls defend against), then `out.data` will not carry `adopted`, so `out.data['adopted']` raises `KeyError: 'adopted'` and the command exits with an uncaught traceback instead of printing the error reason. Even in the benign variant where `out.data` still contains `adopted` (say `0`), the handler still returns exit code 0, so a caller/script sees a successful adoption while the operation actually failed and no reason is ever surfaced to the operator. Demonstrated by running `ddflow session adopt-orphans` in an environment where the backend reports failure: instead of the `out.reason`/non-zero exit that `ddflow session prompt` and `ddflow session start` produce in the same situation, the CLI crashes or reports success.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/knowledge.py:cmd_session (adopt-orphans branch)

titles: ddflow/services/sessions.py — `prompt`, the `sid = harness_session_id(harness_id) or resolve(log)[0]` line

chunk_findings.detail: The count is `len(SS.orphans(events))` minus the *number of distinct* `adopted_from` values, i.e. `len({e.data["adopted_from"] for e in events if e.data.get("adopted_from")})`. Adoption attaches orphans to the nearest session by time, and the natural value for `adopted_from` is that target session id — so several orphan events adopted into the *same* session all share one `adopted_from` value, and the set collapses them to 1. Concretely, with five orphan prompt events all adopted into the single latest open session `S`, `len(orphans)==5` (if `orphans()` still surfaces the adopted events, which is the only reason the subtraction exists) while the set is `{"S"}`, giving `lost = 4`: `ddflow doctor` keeps emitting "4 prompt/note event(s) have no session id" forever even though `adopt-orphans` just fixed them, and re-running the fix cannot clear the note. Conversely, in the reading where `orphans()` already excludes adopted events, the subtraction removes counts that are not in the minuend, so pre-existing adopted events silently cancel genuinely new orphans (3 prior adoptions + 3 fresh orphans → `lost = 0`, no warning). Either way the arithmetic uses the wrong quantity; it must count adopted *events*, not distinct `adopted_from` values, and must not subtract them from a set that already excludes them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting.py:570 `_orphan_notes` (the `lost = ...` computation)

chunk_findings.detail: The docstring states the intended activity order: the clock (`ev.ts`) is primary and "Lamport order breaks a tie in the clock". The code does the opposite — `last` is keyed on `(ev.lamport, ev.ts)`, so Lamport is primary. Whenever the two orders disagree, `live[0]` is not the "most recently active" session and `resolve` returns the wrong "latest" id. Concretely, with two open sessions for the same agent, session A last written at ts `2026-10-02T10:00` with lamport 40 and session B last written at ts `2026-10-02T11:00` with lamport 12, `open_sessions` returns `[A, B]`, `resolve` returns A as "latest", and the prompt/note is recorded in A even though B is the one that was written to last (the module's own `adopt_orphans` orders session starts by `ts`, not by lamport, confirming which field is meant to carry time).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions.py:open_sessions (the `last[...] = max(..., (ev.lamport, ev.ts))` sort key)

chunk_findings.detail: The resolution order required by the change is explicit → harness session id → latest open → implicit, and the docstring of `resolve` says the harness branch is "the session the prompt hook keys on, named by the environment". The implementation only honours the environment id when a matching *started* session already exists (`hid in live`). Given `DDFLOW_SESSION_ID=X` exported for the harness session before any `session.started` event for X has been written (first prompt of the session, or the autocapture hook recorded X under a different agent, so X is not in `live`), `resolve` skips X and either reuses some unrelated open session or opens an implicit session with a fresh random id marked `implicit: True`, even though the harness session is known. The autocapture hook, which keys on X, will then record its own events under X, splitting one harness session across two ddflow sessions and mislabelling the output "(implicit, new)". The guard should only exclude a harness id that is known to be ended, not one that simply has no start event yet.

chunk_findings.detail: The new branch does `out = A.session_adopt_orphans(...)` and then immediately evaluates `f"adopted {out.data['adopted']} orphan(s)"` and returns `OK`, with no `if out.exit != OK:` guard. Concrete failure: on a store that cannot be written (locked DB / IO error) `session_adopt_orphans` returns a non-OK `Result`; if its `data` does not contain `adopted`, the f-string raises `KeyError` and the operator sees a traceback instead of `out.reason`; if `data` happens to contain `{"adopted": 0}`, the CLI prints "adopted 0 orphan(s)" and exits 0, silently masking the failure. In both cases the error that every other `session` subcommand would surface via `out.reason` + `return out.exit` is lost. The command should mirror the surrounding pattern (`if out.exit != OK: print(out.reason ...); return out.exit`) before formatting the success message.

chunk_findings.detail:
The count `lost = len(SS.orphans(events)) - len({e.data["adopted_from"] ...})` cannot be right under either plausible semantics of `orphans`, and it silently suppresses the warning:

1. If adoption does what the intent says ("attaches them to the nearest session", i.e. the event ends up with a session id), then `SS.orphans` no longer returns adopted events. The subset subtraction is therefore applied to events that are *not* in the orphan list and double-counts past adoptions. Concrete: 5 orphans were adopted in an earlier run (`adopted_from` set on those 5), then 2 brand-new orphans appear. `SS.orphans(events)` = 2, the adopted set has 5 distinct values, so `lost = 2 - 5 = -3`, the function returns `[]`, and doctor says nothing about the 2 real orphans that `adopt-orphans` should fix.

2. If instead adopted events are still returned by `orphans` (i.e. they still lack a session id), the subtraction uses a *set* of `adopted_from` values, so several orphans adopted into the same session collapse to one element. Concrete: 2 orphans are adopted into session `S` (both get `adopted_from == "S"`), and no true orphans remain; `orphans` = 2, the set = `{"S"}` size 1, so `lost = 1 > 0` and doctor falsely warns that 1 event still has no session id.

Because `lost <= 0` returns `[]`, case 1 hides the problem entirely rather than misreporting it. The subtraction should either count adopted events by identity (not a set of values) and only among the events `orphans` actually returned, or not subtract at all.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting.py:570-575 (`_orphan_notes`)

chunk_findings.detail: `resolve` promises (docstring and intent) the order explicit → harness → latest open → implicit, and `harness_session_id(...)` is a pure normalizer: the diff's own `prompt` uses it as `harness_session_id(harness_id) or ...` and then creates a `session.started` for `sid` when none exists (`if not any(e.kind == "session.started" and e.subject == sid ...)`), proving it does **not** require the id to correspond to an existing session. But `resolve` only accepts the harness id when it is already in `live` (`if literal and literal in live` / `if hid and hid in live`), i.e. only when a `session.started` for that id already exists. So on the very first prompt/note for a harness session (the exact case the change is meant to support: the hook's session id has no `session.started` yet, or there are only pre-change orphans), the harness id is silently discarded. Given `DDFLOW_SESSION_ID=abc` with no `session.started` for `abc` but an older open session `old`, `resolve` returns `("old", "latest")` instead of `("abc", "harness")`; with no open session it opens a brand-new implicit session id instead of using `abc`. Either way the prompt/note is filed under a session the harness never keyed on, defeating the "else the harness session id the autocapture hook keys on" step. The ended-session rule ("an ended session is never reused") only needs an *ended* check; requiring `in live` additionally rejects never-started harness ids, which the intent says must be used.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions.py :: resolve

chunk_findings.detail:
`_where` returns the string `" -- NOT recorded: session.log_prompts is off"` for `how == "off"`, but the caller unconditionally prefixes its own success word before appending `where`:

- prompt path: `c.out(f"recorded ({out.data['redactions']} redaction(s)){where}", ...)`
- note path: `c.out(f"noted{where}", ...)`

Because `_where(out.data)` is only reached after the `out.exit != OK` guard, the only way the `how == "off"` branch can be hit is with `out.exit == OK`. So with prompt logging disabled, running e.g. `ddflow session prompt --text hi` prints:

`recorded (0 redaction(s)) -- NOT recorded: session.log_prompts is off`

and `ddflow session note --text hi` prints `noted -- NOT recorded: session.log_prompts is off`. Both lines assert the text *was* recorded ("recorded"/"noted") and then immediately assert it was *not* recorded, in the very same message. A user or script parsing the first word is told the prompt/note was stored when the backend explicitly reports it was dropped. The `off` case needs to suppress the "recorded"/"noted" prefix (or replace it), not append a negation to it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/knowledge.py:`_where` / `cmd_session` (prompt & note)
